Fundamental Concepts: Abiotic and biotic components of ecosystems
Levels of biological organization (individuals, population, species, community, ecosystems, biomes)
Interactions: Types of interactions (mutualism, symbiosis, commensalism, competition, parasitism, predation, etc.)
Trophic levels and their direct and indirect interactions
Community Ecology: Role of dispersal and habitat/environmental filtering
Species richness, Evenness and diversity indices
Diversity gradients (e.g. latitudinal and altitudinal gradients)
Ecosystem Structure and Function: Food web, energy flow, and biogeochemical cycles (e.g. carbon and nitrogen)

Fundamentals: Types of selection (e.g. stabilizing, directional, disruptive)
Diversity of Life: Origin and history of life on earth
Population and Quantitative Genetics: Population genetic structure (panmixia, gene flow, FST)
Molecular Evolution and Phylogenetics: Chromosomal and genome evolution (e.g. hybridization, ploidy, introgression)
Phylogenetic methods (parsimony; maximum likelihood, Bayesian, etc)

Mathematics and Statistics in Ecology: Simple functions (linear, quadratic, exponential, logarithmic, etc)
Concept of derivatives and slope of a function
Basic probability (probability of random events; Sequences of events, conditional probability, etc)
Descriptive statistics (mean, variance, coefficient of variation, confidence intervals, etc.)
Study design and Statistical methods: Type I and Type II error

Classical Ethology and Sensory Ecology: Proximate and ultimate explanations for behaviour
Foraging and Reproduction: Sexual selection and sexual conflict (runaway selection, good-genes, handicap principle, etc)

Biodiversity and Conservation: Global conservation initiatives (e.g. COP, IUCN, CBD, CITES)
Conservation genetics and methods (genetic diversity, inbreeding depression, DNA fingerprinting and DNA barcoding)
Global Change: Causes, consequences, adaptation and mitigation of climate change
Threats to biodiversity (e.g. pollution, habitat loss and change)
